title: Stride-aware kernel selector and prefill-slice optimizer for FlashAttention v2/v3
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce a stride-aware kernel selection layer plus a prefill-slice optimizer that selects between FlashAttention v2 and v3 kernels based on token stride patterns, KV cache reuse potential, and decode boundary alignment. The feature aims to reduce p99 prefill latency regressions observed on long-context workloads while preserving decode throughput.
background: We have recurring regressions when switching between FA2 and FA3 for long prefill requests. Current kernel selector uses coarse heuristics (sequence length and batch size) and misses cases with high stride (sparse attention windows, windowed context hops) causing suboptimal memory layout and kernel thrashing. Customers running long-context retrieval and multi-doc concatenation see p99 spikes and occasional OOMs during prefill bursts.
goal: 1) Build a lightweight stride estimator in the runtime that computes an expected stride distribution for incoming prefill request groups; 2) Use the estimator in a selector that picks FA2 vs FA3 and memory tiling configs; 3) Implement prefill-slice optimizer that reorders slices to maximize KV reuse and reduce workspace churn.
decisions: Prefer a runtime-only solution (no model changes) to keep customer migration friction low.
Selector will be conservative: if stride estimate is ambiguous, prefer FA2 for safety and memory predictability.
Optimizer will be opt-in via route config initially; default remains existing selector to minimize blast radius.
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Spike completed — implemented stride histogram prototype and validated estimator accuracy on internal replay traces (10k requests). Observed that high-stride workloads are ~12% of traffic but account for ~28% of prefill p99s.
2026-03-04: Selector prototype wired into runtime decision path; added feature flag and per-request telemetry tags (selector.choice, stride.mean, stride.95).
2026-03-06: Canary run on dev cluster showed 6% p99 prefill reduction for the targeted route, but noticed a small (1.5%) increase in mean workspace allocations when FA3 chosen incorrectly.
2026-03-08: Reproduced OOM scenario in local harness with skewed stride histogram; added fallback to pre-allocate lower memory layout when allocation fails.
2026-03-10: Began A/B canary (10% traffic) on staging routes; collecting memory/latency and regression signals.
acceptance_criteria: Canary on staging shows >=10% reduction in target route p99 prefill latency without increasing p50 more than 5%.
No increase in OOMs across canary traffic; any allocation fallback must not exceed 2% error budget for route.
Telemetry emitted for selector decisions and optimizer reorder counts; dashboards created in Grafana and linked.
Implementation gated behind an opt-in route flag and documented in runtime rollout playbook.
tasks: Implement stride estimator module and unit tests (runtime library).
Add kernel selector interface to compare FA2 vs FA3 cost model using stride input.
Implement prefill-slice optimizer that can reorder contiguous slices to maximize KV reuse.
Add telemetry hooks: selector.choice, stride.percentiles, optimizer.reorders, fallback_reason.
Run offline simulation against 1M trace samples to tune thresholds and duty-cycle for selector.
Create staging canary and dashboards; coordinate with SRE for resource knobs and rollback playbook.
Write docs and developer guide for enabling route opt-in and expected metrics to monitor.
notes: Trade-off: more conservative selection reduces regressions but may miss some FA3 throughput wins on medium-stride workloads.
If canary detects kernel oscillation (rapid flips between FA2/FA3) we will enable a sticky decision window per connection for 30s.
Plan B: if memory footprint with FA3 remains unpredictable, fall back to a prefill-only FA2 execution path until a full allocator redesign is scheduled.
Owner will coordinate a post-mortem if any production rollout causes >5% error budget burn for a route.
